BiblicalUsage: It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe quietly waiting is the hardest kind of hope: not the waiting that paces and demands, but the waiting that sits still because it trusts the Lord to come.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
